To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of Rls specific for the lactating period is highly justified.

RIs for hematological, biochemical and acute phase protein parameters in Holstein dairy cattle should be different for cows in early lactation compared to those in mid lactation, and that the day of sampling should be taken into consideration for the determination of some analytes, especially for those related to the oxidative stress.

RIs for hematological and biochemistry analytes, acute phase proteins (APP) and oxidation markers in Holstein dairy cow blood are significantly different between the first 3 and the last 30 days of lactation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of RIs for a large number of analytes in Holstein cows in two different lactation periods.
the establishment of RIs for a wide range of analytes in dairy cows at two different lactation periods.
the determination of RAs for a large number of hematological, biochemical, inflammatory and oxidation markers in dairy cows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of RIS specific for the lactational period is highly justified, but the adoption of RIs specific to other factors (parity or management) is not practical.
the use of a single RI for all cows, regardless of the lactation stage, should be discouraged.
RIs specific for lactation period are highly justified and should be adopted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RIs should be specific for the lactational period and that the use of specific RIs, for the different parities or for the different management systems, should be evaluated on a case by case basis.
the establishment of RIs for dairy cows should take into account the lactation period.
RIs should not be applied in a rigid manner and that the clinical relevance of the results should always be taken into consideration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of RIS for dairy cows in the first 3days of lactation is advisable, as well as in the subsequent weeks of lactation.
the use of specific reference intervals for dairy cows at different stages of lactation is highly justified from the statistical as well as from the biological point of view.
the use of specific RIs is highly justified in the evaluation of laboratory data in dairy cows, especially in the evaluation of metabolic and inflammation markers.
